stories.text: `implement` must support explicit single mode for code implementation, run in a single process, avoid team worker lanes and tmux HUD, and still continue to formal review, qa, and gate.

`implement` must support explicit team mode, enter a bounded multi-agent runtime, produce role reports, worker evidence, tmux panes, and HUD, while keeping canonical writeback owned by Beacon stage owner.
`ralph` must operate only around the implement plus qa closure, must not rewrite frozen prd, user-story, or test-case materials directly, and must expose explicit stop states.
`qa` must act as the second execution plane after implement, covering browser acceptance, boundary discovery, structure inference, and repair handoff instead of a one-shot trailing test pass.
`qa` must execute in frozen material order, reading frozen prd, frozen user-story, and frozen test-case before browser scenarios, and must not expand scope beyond those frozen inputs.

`qa` must launch a real browser environment for the target project and support a browser execution family that includes browser-cli, agent-browser, pageagent, and browser-use for page and flow validation.
`qa` must support ordered, multi-round browser scenario execution where each round can reprioritize the next set of browser checks based on the previous round findings.
Every qa round must add new auto research value such as a new browser boundary, a new page state, a new exception path, a new coverage closure, or a new repair handoff.
Each qa round must output boundary feedback, flow or page structure inference, uncovered scope notes, and feed that evidence into repair handoff or the next Ralph decision.
Multi-round qa must progressively polish functional correctness, browser acceptance path completeness, and product boundary clarity instead of replaying the same page script without learning.
`ralph` must support at least release_ready, human_blocked, and budget_exhausted stop states and decide continuation only from formal implement, qa, and gate outputs.
`status` and `help` must display the current mode, current round, current browser runner or executor, current blocker, and recommended next step for the active implement or qa loop.
`v1.3.2` must continue the minimal human workflow and keep `prd -> user-story -> test-case -> implement -> qa -> release` as the stable public cognitive loop.
`v1.3.2` must not add new public top-level commands that force humans to operate team, subagent, or precheck flows directly.
When Beacon runs as a skill inside Codex or Claude, it must use the host-native subagent or team capability instead of bridging another external executor; `omx` remains a design reference only.
`runtime-readiness` and `delegation-readiness` prechecks must be embedded into `implement` and `qa` by default and must not become extra daily commands that humans need to remember.
Precheck, delegation, and blocker decisions must expose minimal human-facing output while preserving detailed machine-readable diagnostics for automation and audit.

`v1.3.2` must treat the current host context as unique and only decide whether the active host supports native subagent or team capability; it must not introduce multi-runtime bridge or selection semantics.
